title: Speed first build plan
eyebrow: Build plan · design approved 2026-11-24 · nothing built yet

short.lead: Six steps, issues #626 to #631 under parent issue #625, make every hook call and the test suite faster, each timed before and after. The build plan is the contract: I log each departure from it and list them in the final report.
short.hint: Tap a group to see its steps. The Changes section below gives each step's files and done-test.

changes: chg
Step 1: timing script (issue #626)
A script that prints milliseconds per call and saves a baseline.

Done when: one command times a Write and a Bash hook call, the 5 label reads, the Stop judge and each verify.py part, and saves the baseline; a check in tools/verify_tools.py runs it. Touches tools/time_hooks.py and tools/verify_tools.py. Depends on nothing; steps 2 to 6 depend on it. Also touches CHANGELOG.md.

changes.alt: Diagram: a stopwatch beside a list of hook calls with milliseconds.
changes.caption: A script that prints milliseconds per call and saves a baseline.

changes: chg
Step 2: load only the needed part (issue #627)
hook.py imports one module per event instead of all seven.
Done when: the timing script shows a lower per-call time than the baseline and verify.py passes in full. Touches scripts/hook.py. Depends on step 1. Also touches CHANGELOG.md.

changes.alt: Diagram: nine heavy hook boxes becoming light ones.
changes.caption: hook.py imports one module per event instead of all seven.

changes: chg
Step 3: one process per phase (issue #628)
Checks before a tool call share one process; checks after share another.

Done when: a Write starts 2 processes instead of 9 and a Bash call 2 instead of 6, the timing script shows a lower per-call time than step 2's number for both, the worst-case merged run stays under the 10 second limit, and verify.py passes in full. Each merged check keeps the failure rule it has today (listed in the issue before the build), and a test crashes one blocking check and one other check to prove both. Touches hooks/hooks.json, scripts/hook.py and CHANGELOG.md. Depends on step 2.

changes.alt: Diagram: nine hook processes joined into two boxes.
changes.caption: Checks before a tool call share one process; checks after share another.

changes: chg
Step 4: label reads, profile then fix (issue #629)
The 5 reads already run in a thread pool; this step profiles a real gate call, then fixes the cause.

Finding: the 5 reads already run in a thread pool (design_loop.py:826), so the 748 ms came from reading them one at a time by hand. Done when: the timing script shows where a real gate call spends its time, and the fix brings the label reads to about one read (about 150 ms) with GitHub still read on every call (decision 2026-10-14, docs/6-decisions/Decisions.md); if the pool already gives that, the step closes with the measured number and no code change. Touches scripts/house_rules/design_loop.py, its tests and CHANGELOG.md. Depends on step 1.

changes.alt: Diagram from the proposal: five label reads one after another (748 ms), then a faster option. The review found the reads already run in a pool, so this shows the proposal's assumption, not today's code.
changes.caption: The commit gate's 5 reads run in a thread pool; GitHub is read every call.

changes: chg
Step 5: append-only hook log (issue #630)
The hook log adds one line per write and is trimmed under a lock.

Done when: a test with parallel writers loses no line, a crash mid-trim leaves the log readable, the timing script shows the log write costs less than the baseline, and verify.py passes in full. Touches the hook log code in scripts/house_rules/core.py, its tests and CHANGELOG.md. Depends on step 1.

changes.alt: Diagram: whole-file rewrites becoming one-line appends.
changes.caption: One line appended per write; trimmed under a lock.

changes: chg
Step 6: easy test wins (issue #631)
Quick, safe speedups to verify.py chosen from step 1's timings.

Done when: verify.py's total time falls against the baseline, the list of check names printed by verify.py is identical before and after, and what is left for the code-quality phase is listed in the issue. Step 6 also bumps the plugin version and sets hook-speed.md status to built, and it runs last. Touches scripts/checks/common.py, the parts the timings point to and CHANGELOG.md. Depends on step 1.
chg
Acceptance tests (all steps)
One test per design item, run by the reviewer in acceptance mode before QA.

Done when: each passes with its evidence saved under docs/qa/speed-first/: design item 1 (scope): the timing script shows lower numbers than the baseline for a Write call, a Bash call and the log; design item 2 (labels): the 5 reads run at the same time (already true) and GitHub is still read every call; design item 3 (judge): the judge's code is unchanged in the diff and the script prints its time; design item 4 (tests): verify.py total time is lower than the baseline with the same list of check names. Plus a closing check, not a design item: version, hook-speed.md status, CHANGELOG.md lines and a full verify.py pass. These are the design's four choices, not the build steps.
